newsitem.title: USA: U.S., in retaliation, expels Belarus diplomat.
newsitem.headline: U.S., in retaliation, expels Belarus diplomat.

text.p: The United States on Wednesday expelled a diplomat from Belarus in retaliation for similar action taken against an American diplomat in Minsk.

"The United States has informed Belarus that Vladimir Gramyka, first secretary and consul, has been declared persona non grata," State Department spokesman John Dinger told reporters. Gramyka was given 24 hours to leave the country.
"Mr. Gramyka is being expelled in retaliation for the unwarranted and unjust expulsion March 24 of the first secretary at the U.S. Embassy in Minsk," he said.
The tit-for-tat expulsion responded to last weekend's arrest in Minsk by Belarus authorities of the first secretary at the U.S. Embassy there, Serzh Alexandrov.
Alexandrov, who is of Belarussian origin, was detained at an opposition rally protesting against the pro-Moscow policies of hardline President Alexander Lukashenko.
Belarus accused him of "provocative" actions. The embassy said he was carrying out his normal diplomatic duties.

Gramyka was chosen for expulsion because he is of the equivalent rank and status as Alexandrov. The terms of his expulsion -- 24 hours -- are also the same as Belarus imposed on the American diplomat. The families of both men have been given more time to depart.
Dinger expressed concern about the deterioration in U.S.-Belarus ties but did not rule out further action by Washington.

U.S. relations with Belarus have worsened sharply in recent weeks. Washington has been a vociferous opponent of Lukashenko's increasingly authoritarian rule with Dinger reiterating: "We remain deeply concerned by the accelerating slide to authoritarianism in Belarus."
On Tuesday, the State Department recalled its ambassador to Belarus for consultations. Last week, it cut off $40 million in aid because of Minsk's human rights record.
